headline_marked: Kushtia: [[MP Amir Hamza's car vandalized]] during clash between supporters
headline: Kushtia: MP Amir Hamza's car vandalized during clash between supporters
summary: Supporters of MP Amir Hamza and members of Gono Odhikar Parishad clashed in Kushtia, leaving several injured and a vehicle damaged.
details: A violent clash broke out between the supporters of MP Amir Hamza and members of the Gono Odhikar Parishad in Kushtia city. The incident occurred at the Choy Rasta intersection on Saturday afternoon.

Jamaat leaders alleged that Gono Odhikar Parishad activists vandalized MP Hamza's car and injured 8 to 10 of their workers. They claimed the attack was pre-planned and threatened on Facebook beforehand.

Conversely, Gono Odhikar Parishad leaders claimed their peaceful protest against derogatory remarks made by the MP was disrupted by his supporters. They further alleged that Jamaat activists later attacked their district office and local businesses.

Police were present at the scene and attempted to calm the situation. Additional Superintendent of Police Faisal Mahmud stated that legal action will be taken against those involved based on the decision of senior officials.
Both Gono Odhikar Parishad and Jamaat-e-Islami have announced their intention to file legal cases regarding the attacks and vandalism.

headline: PM Tarique Rahman gas crisis to end in a few days, load shedding persists
summary: The Prime Minister expressed regret for the load shedding and stated that the electricity situation will improve once the gas shortage is resolved.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expressed regret to the nation for the ongoing load shedding and load shedding. He stated that if everything goes as planned, the gas crisis will be resolved within a few days, which will subsequently improve the power situation.

Speaking at an event in Dhaka's Mohakhali T&T field on Saturday, the PM emphasized that the previous government's 'mega-corruption' and failure to drill new gas wells up until the last moment had led to the current crisis.
He criticized critics of the current administration, calling their complaints 'reckless' and urged them those who are critical to provide actual solutions instead of creating confusion.
The PM mentioned that the government is working on establishing a third LNG terminal to solve the long-term crisis, though he noted that building the infrastructure would take time.
He further stated that the government has been in discussions with China and Malaysia to resolve the immediate gas shortage.
Tarique Rahman also challenged the opposition, stating that if they can provide a solution to the gas and electricity crisis within three to six months, the government will accept it.
He urged political parties to avoid the 'politics of confusion' and present a plan that benefits the people of Bangladesh.
He noted that the current government has only been in power for six months and is working to implement its electoral promises to the people.
He criticized the previous fascist government for leaving behind a debt of 3 lakh crore Taka in the power sector,
